messages:
alex: quick FYI — canary 2030123 on h100s shows a p95 latency jump for short contexts after we enabled segmented-queue routing.
maria: saw that. p50 stable but p95 +12ms on short ctx (<64). link to traces: https://internal/traces/2030123
sam: any repro? which metric shows kernel swap cost? or is it batching heuristic causing misroute?
alex: initial profiling attached below. prefill path avg token-time 3.9ms, decode path 6.1ms when running native kernels. but when autotune switches kernel for longctx the shortctx requests get misrouted and see ~5.6ms kernel-swap overhead.
lee: paste of profiling snippet (copied from run):
```
# profile summary (shortctx slot)
prefill: kernel=v1_matmul_fast, avg=3.9ms
decode: kernel=v2_matmul_mixed, avg=6.1ms
swap penalty: 5.6ms (context switch + kv-load)
kv-hit-rate: 78% -> 52% after canary
```
alex: kv-hit-rate drop looks correlated with bursty traffic — autotune uses global seqlen histogram and picks decode path that favors longctx throughput, but that hurts short ctx.
maria: is this Ampere vs H100 specific? canary was on h100, prev stable on ampere.
sam: runtime-autotune picks are architecture-aware but we found an edge where scoring function overweights long-token throughput for h100. result: choose fused-kernel that has higher startup cost.
lee: proposed quick mitigation: change routing policy to prefer short-path sticky routing for sequences < 64 until kv-hit-rate stabilizes. Also add a guarded cooldown so autotune doesn't flip kernels more than once per 90s per host.
alex: agree. for immediate rollback I'll flip canary to use legacy routing policy and revert kernel pick on the h100 pool.
infra-bot: deploy request: rollback routing-policy -> legacy for pool=h100-canary by @alex
maria: also add a perf test that simulates kv-eviction bursts: script below to run locally
```
# simulate burst that thrashes kv cache
python perf/sim_kv_thrash.py --clients 300 --avg_len 16 --burst 5m
```
sam: small config patch to try before full rollback — reduce longctx weight in autotune scoring from 1.2 -> 0.9 and add sticky short-path threshold 0.6
```
autotune:
  longctx_weight: 0.9
  sticky_short_threshold: 0.6
  cooldown_seconds: 90
```
lee: will run canary with that patch on 2 hosts. if p95 improves we keep. if not, rollback.
alex: can you also collect kernel switch traces + NVTX spans? we need exact cost distribution across cpu<->gpu copy, kernel init, kv reload.
maria: adding NVTX and extended logging for next run. also adding a metric for 'kernel_switch_count' per minute.
sam: curious: why did kv-hit-rate drop to 52%? initial look suggests parallel requests bypassed suffix-level cache because of batching alignment shift.
lee: yes, the batching heuristic aligned more aggressively for longctx and ended up evicting short prefixes earlier. fix idea: batch alignment policy should respect prefix-skew ratio for shortctx-heavy workloads.
alex: action items:
- lee: run canary with autotune patch + NVTX spans (1h) — due in 30m
- maria: add perf sim and kernel_switch_count metric — due EOD
- sam: roll back canary to legacy routing if p95 not improved in 1h
- infra-bot: record deploy + rollback events
maria: noted. will open a quick PR with metric + sim. link: https://git/internal/pulls/9812
alex: thanks. moving to watch channel for the next hour. :eyes:
